title: 5 Best OCR Solutions for KYC and KYB Processing
summary: Discover top OCR tools for accurate, secure KYC/KYB document processing: AnyCheck by Fintelite, Koncile, Doxis, Docsumo, and Ondato.
body_markdown:
Most OCR tools just convert an image into text. For KYC/KYB regulated processes, you need an intelligent OCR that can accurately handle the different document formats customers submit, keep sensitive data secure, and output standardized fields your compliance team can actually use. This is where generic OCR tools often fall short.


This guide lists the 5 best OCR tools to support a more efficient KYC and KYB process. Each is evaluated based on accuracy, document coverage, and deployment options.


## **What OCR Does in KYC vs KYB**


OCR (Optical Character Recognition) is a technology that reads, extracts, and converts information from images or documents into machine-readable data. Before performing any compliance check, customer documents have to be turned into a structured data format systems can work with. With OCR, that happens automatically, capturing all the necessary customer data compliance teams need instead of someone copying them by hand.


In practice, OCR plays a different role depending on whether you’re verifying a person or a business. For KYC, it extracts personal identity data from documents like passports, ID cards, and driver’s licenses. For KYB, it extracts entity data from business documents like incorporation certificates and ownership registers. This structured data can then support further compliance checks, including[anti-money laundering (AML)](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/aml.asp) screening.


## **Essential OCR Capabilities for KYC and KYB Process**


KYC and KYB come with strict requirements around accuracy, security, and documentation. To ensure a smooth, compliant implementation, evaluate OCR tools based on these must-haves:


### Custom data extraction to institutional requirements


Every institution has different document types, formats, and data fields it needs to capture. Look for OCR that can be configured to your specific requirements for optimal implementation.


### High, consistent accuracy


OCR needs to deliver high accuracy across the board, not just on easy, clean documents. Precision matters most on the fields compliance actually depends on, like ID numbers, names, and dates, since even small errors there can cause a false match or missed flag.


### Scalability across varying formats


Documents rarely follow a single layout.[Bank statements](https://fintelite.ai/bank-statement-extraction-and-how-to-use-it-for-your-business/) alone can vary widely from bank to bank, and KYB submissions bring even more inconsistency. The OCR needs to handle that variation without losing accuracy.


### Data security and deployment


Since these documents contain sensitive personal and financial information, where and how the data is processed matters. Some tools offer[on-premise or cloud](https://fintelite.ai/on-premise-vs-cloud-ocr/) processing, including client-side options that keep documents within your environment.


### Integration with existing workflows


Does it plug into your AML screening, case management, or onboarding system, or does it just output raw text you still have to route manually?

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


****What types of KYC and KYB documents can OCR process?****


For KYC, OCR typically handles passports, national ID cards, driver’s licenses, and proof of address documents. For KYB, it covers certificates of incorporation, business licenses, articles of association, beneficial ownership (UBO) registers, and tax identification documents.


****Can OCR be deployed on-premise into our existing systems ?****


Yes. Most OCR providers offer API access for direct integration into onboarding platforms, case management systems, or internal tools. AnyCheck by Fintelite also supports on-premise installation for teams with stricter infrastructure requirements.


****Can OCR handle bulk document processing?****


Yes, most compliance-grade OCR tools support batch processing so teams can handle large volumes of documents at once. This is especially useful for KYB reviews or clearing a backlog.


****How long does OCR take to implement?****


It depends on the provider and deployment type. Cloud-based OCR with API/SDK access can often be integrated within a day to a few days, while on-premise deployments or highly customized setups (specific field configurations, unique document templates) typically take longer, from a few weeks to a couple of months.


****Can OCR output be customized to fit our workflow?****


Yes, many OCR tools let you configure which fields get extracted and how the output is formatted, whether that’s JSON, CSV, or a direct feed into your existing case management or onboarding system.
